prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup
Asset type: high-fidelity 16:9 desktop documentation homepage design comp for an open-source Dart terminal UI framework
Primary request: Design the first viewport and the beginning of the second fold for Noir documentation as a type-foundry terminal proof sheet. The page must unmistakably be a usable documentation website, not a poster.
Structure: A narrow, precise top navigation with NOIR at left and Docs, Guides, API, Examples, GitHub at right. Below it, a giant authentic 80×24 terminal frame occupies roughly the left two-thirds of the viewport and is the single dominant focal artifact. A right annotation margin traces the frame through three labeled layers: Widget, Element, RenderObject. A compact quick-start strip on the baseline contains the exact command "$ dart pub add noir" and two actions, "Get started" and "Read the guides". Show the beginning of the next fold as a continuous section with three reading paths, without enclosing them in generic cards.
Content: Exact headline "Flutter-like widgets for terminal apps." Supporting line "Build reactive terminal interfaces in Dart, rendered by OpenTUI." Include the architecture line "Widgets declare. Elements preserve identity. RenderObjects layout and record paint." The terminal specimen should visibly render a crisp Noir example with title, body text, a simple counter, a focused action, and cell rulers.
Style/medium: Editorial web UI comp informed by type-foundry proof sheets, press registration marks, annotated engineering proofs, and real terminal capture sheets. Warm proof paper ground, near-black registration ink, signal-coral active marks, pale blue editorial annotations. Proportional grotesk for reading text; monospace only for code, terminal cells, measurements, and labels. Hairline rules, crop marks, baseline measurements, and margin notes provide the component language.
Composition/framing: 2048×1152 landscape, full browser viewport, strict asymmetrical editorial grid, no floating mock device, no isolated hero card. Show enough below the fold to prove this can become a full documentation system.
Interaction implied: A small SOURCE / FRAME / TREE view control integrated into the specimen rail, with FRAME active using a solid registration mark rather than a pill.
Constraints: Professional open-source documentation; candid prerelease signal "0.0.1-alpha.3" near the brand; excellent hierarchy and readable code; no invented adoption metrics, testimonials, benchmarks, or company logos; all visible text must be spelled correctly; use no more text than specified.
Avoid: green-on-black hacker styling, neon glow, glass, gradients, rounded bento cards, generic SaaS hero, fake terminal window traffic-light dots, excessive monospace body copy, decorative grids, emoji, stock illustration, gradient text, shadows, device mockups, watermarks.
